I'd like to preface this by saying some of the details I include will be purposely ambiguous in the event someone has to go to traffic court with this vigilante heroine. I say someone, because the person in the story isn't even me, but it will be told in first person, regardless. By the way, the person in this story has a clean driving record.

There I was, crawling through an unfamiliar parking lot at less than 5 mph in my vehicle.There were no other cars around me that were not parked. A very large woman hails me and I stop and roll down my window, wondering if she possibly needed some help or if she just wanted to confess her undying love for me, or whatever. I greet her with a smile, like I'm working at McDonald's, and ask how I can help her. Her eyes are stone, and I can tell that this portly woman is only too happy that I have allowed her to create a situation by stopping and engaging her.

"This is a insert potential traffic violation here street."

"Oh! I did not see any signs. Thank you for telling me, though, I will keep it in mind for next time."

I figure that's that, but no, she's still trying to laser me with her eyes. It almost works, because I am generally a calm a person, but I can feel myself flush a bit, a little bit of heat, because, surely, this fat bitch is not trying to intimidate me. I continue to smile into her eyeballs, making sure that I don't break eye contact to allow her some pleasurable feeling of canine dominance. "I understand," I say firmly.

"Then you should back up," she drools.

I allow another friendly smirk to paint my face, "No, I think I'll go through."

"I'm gonna' have to contact the state police," she warbles, her neck slapping itself between syllables.

I communicate to her that that is likely the best course of action, "You do that," and I slowly continue on my way as she crams her meaty fist into her pocket to retrieve her phone for a photo of my car and tags.

Just an aside, I'm sure some of you were in the military, but it is kind of a universal thing if you replace "Marine" with "you": when I heard "Hey, Marine!" while I was in, I learned to not look back. Hearing "Hey, Marine!" meant someone was about to get tasked with some tedious bullshit or that someone was going to get their ass chewed. If you looked back, it was you.

The lesson to both of these stories is always act oblivious. Do not give strangers the time of day. People have this weird sense of entitlement and a longing to exert control over others even from outside of a position of authority, I am sure I'm preaching to the choir on Voat, though.
